title: Postmortem communication playbook and bridge checklist
content:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight runbook for how we communicate during and after incidents, with: (1) status page templates tuned to incident stage and customer impact, (2) customer-facing email and in-product banner examples, and (3) an internal war-room / bridge checklist and scripts for the bridge lead and on-call.

Design goals
- Fast, consistent messaging: minimize cognitive load for the bridge lead when time is short.
- Tiered transparency: match message detail to audience (public status page vs enterprise email vs internal Slack).
- Actionable handoffs: ensure the postmortem comms loop completes (notify customers, publish root cause and mitigations).

Roles & responsibilities (quick)
- Bridge lead: run comm cadence, own public status updates, call customer comms when needed.
- Incident commander (IC): owns mitigation, ETA, and technical updates.
- Communications lead: drafts customer-facing copy and coordinates legal/PR for high-impact incidents.
- Account lead / CSM: owns direct customer outreach for impacted enterprise customers.
- SRE on-call: executes mitigation steps and provides technical status.

Notification matrix (who to contact first)
- Sev 1 (service down affecting >10% of customers or critical tenants):
  - Pager to on-call SRE, immediate call to bridge lead and IC.
  - CC communications lead, Head of SRE, Product PM.
  - Notify CSMs for top 20 enterprise customers in parallel.
- Sev 2 (degraded performance, partial outage):
  - Pager to on-call, async notification to bridge lead and IC.
  - Communications lead and CSMs on standby.

Status page templates (short, staged, copyable)
Template rules: keep <200 words; include impact, scope, what we are doing, ETA if known, links to workarounds and incident ticket. Update at least every 30 minutes for Sev1 until in monitoring.

1) Investigating (initial public):
Title: Investigating: increased error rates for Redwood API
Body: We are currently investigating reports of increased errors and elevated latencies for the Redwood API. Some requests are failing with 5xx errors and some customers may see higher response times. Our engineers are actively investigating. We will post an update within 30 minutes or sooner. Impact: API requests may fail or be slow for a subset of customers. Internal ticket: INC-1234.

2) Identified (root cause / mitigation underway):
Title: Partial outage identified — degraded generation latency
Body: We identified a configuration regression in the request routing layer that is causing a subset of GPU nodes to be overloaded, leading to increased latency and failures for some requests. Engineers have disabled the problematic routing policy and are rebalancing traffic to healthy capacity. Workaround: retrying failed requests or reducing batch size reduces error rates for most customers. ETA for mitigation: 45 minutes.

3) Mitigating / Monitoring (near-resolution):
Title: Mitigation in progress — performance improving
Body: Mitigations are in place and overall request success rate is improving. We continue to monitor traffic and performance; customers should see reductions in errors and latency. We will update again when all traffic has stabilized.

4) Resolved (post-incident):
Title: Resolved: Redwood API performance restored
Body: The issue impacting API availability has been resolved. Traffic has returned to normal and all services are operating within expected parameters. We are completing a post-incident review and will publish a follow-up summary within 72 hours that includes root cause and preventive actions.

Customer-facing comms (examples)
Guidance: For enterprise customers, send an email within 2 hours for Sev1 incidents and include specific tenant impact, workaround, ETA, and what we will do next. For developer-facing messages, update status.redwood.ai and post a short thread in #status-updates.

Enterprise email template (concise)
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API — status update
Body: Hi <Customer Name>,
We want to let you know that we are currently responding to an incident that may have impacted API requests for your account. What we saw: increased error rates and elevated latency affecting a subset of requests between HH:MM and HH:MM UTC. What we are doing: our SRE team identified a routing configuration regression and is rebalancing traffic to healthy nodes. Immediate impact and workaround: you may see transient failures — retries with exponential backoff should succeed; lowering batch size reduces errors. ETA: we expect mitigation within ~45 minutes.
We will follow up with a full incident summary once our postmortem is complete. If you need real-time updates or escalations, reply to this email or contact your CSM.
Thanks for your patience,
Asha Patel
Head of Incident Communications

In-product banner (short)
We recommend: single-line message + link to status page.
Banner text: We are investigating elevated errors and latency for the Redwood API. View status updates: https://status.redwood.ai/inc-1234

Internal war-room / bridge checklist (play-by-play)
Before bridge opens (first 5 minutes)
- Confirm alert (logs, dashboards).
- Create incident ticket (Jira INC-1234) with impact, initial evidence, and severity.
- Bridge lead: open bridge (Zoom/signal/Google Meet), invite IC, on-call SRE, communications lead, and product PM. Post meeting link to #sre-bridge (pinned).

First 15 minutes (stabilize communications)
- Put up initial status page entry (use Investigating template).
- Bridge lead assigns roles and cadence (e.g., update every 15–30 min).
- Communications lead drafts enterprise email if Sev1, shares in bridge for signoff (within 10m).
- Appoint customer point contacts (CSM) and identify top impacted tenants.

Ongoing (every update window)
- IC provides current hypothesis, actions taken, and next ETA.
- Bridge lead posts public status update and internal summary to #sre-bridge.
- Communications lead posts to CSMs and prepares external email for approval if scope widens.

Escalation steps (when to escalate beyond bridge)
- If >2 hours and no meaningful improvement, involve Head of SRE + CTO + Legal for potential regulatory/PR implications.
- If specific enterprise tenant SLA is violated, account lead must be looped immediately and a follow-up compensation discussion scheduled.

Bridge lead script (quick snippets)
- Opening: "We have an active incident: keyword: API errors. Current scope: X% of requests affected. IC: please give a 1-minute summary and hypothesis."
- Update: "Short update: action taken since last update, current signal (errors down/up), next ETA, any customer-facing changes."
- Closing: "We are moving to monitoring; next update in 60 minutes, and we will publish a full postmortem within 72 hours."

Post-incident communications checklist
- Publish a 'resolved' status page update.
- Send targeted enterprise follow-up email (within 24 hours) with: timeline, root cause summary, mitigations deployed, next steps, and contact for support.
- Draft postmortem (owner: IC) and share for review (72 hours).
- Communications lead prepares a short public postmortem summary for status.redwood.ai and optional blog post if customer-visible impact was large.

Templates for postmortem summary (public):
Title: Incident summary — API routing regression (YYYY-MM-DD)
Body: Summary of impact, root cause (configuration/regression), actions taken, and permanent corrective actions (change to routing validation, automated checks, more conservative rollout policy). Expected follow-up: timeline for deployment of preventative measures.

Metrics & closure criteria
- Incident considered closed when: public status is "resolved", enterprise customers notified, and postmortem draft published for triage.
- Measure: time to first public update, update cadence adherence, time to resolution, % of customers requiring follow-up.

Example quick links to include in updates
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1234
- Bridge link: (post in #sre-bridge)
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/inc-1234

Open questions and drafts
- Determine SLA for posting enterprise emails for Sev2 incidents (proposal: notify top 50 accounts for Sev2 if errors exceed 5 minutes and impact >5% of requests).
- Draft automation: create a template generator that fills in error rate, affected regions, and ETA from monitoring signals to speed first update.

Appendix: quick copy snippets
- One-line public: "Investigating elevated errors affecting a subset of API requests; engineers are investigating. More updates in 30 minutes."
- Two-line public: "Identified routing regression causing spikes in error rates. Mitigation underway; ETA ~45 minutes."
- Customer reassurance: "We recognize the impact and are prioritizing restoration for affected customers. If you need support, contact your CSM."

Notes and provenance
- Created from previous SRE war-room templates and post-incident learnings (2023–2024). Intended as an operational draft — please suggest edits in the doc's comments.
